newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee called to open little changed.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee called to open little changed.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures were called to open little changed on Friday, although some traders expected the market to follow-through on Thursday's tumble to three-month lows.
"I am anticipating some follow-through selling," said one trader, who added a rise in certified stocks and mild weather in top-grower Brazil were likelt to continue to weigh on sentiment.

CSCE reported after Thursday's close that certified coffee inventories rose for the fifth day in a row, increasing by 4,321 60-kg bags as of July 9, to 66,115 bags. An additional 31,959 bags were pending grading, the exchange said.

On the weather front, U.S.-based forecaster Weather Services Corp said on Friday that there was no damaging cold in sight for Brazil's coffee belt, with favorable weather for the ongoing harvest expected during the next several days.

Thursday, New York arabica futures fell sharply on speculative selling amid a build-up in exchange-certified stocks, continued mild weather in top-grower Brazil and a reaffirmation by the USDA of a 28 million bag 1997/98 Brazil coffee crop.

Benchmark September arabicas tumbled 15.35 cents, to 161.70 cents, after ranging between 178.00 and 160.00. Spot July fell 14.50 cents, to 182.50 cents, while the back months finished 0.75 to 4.20 cents lower.
The July/September switch widened to 20.80 cents compared with 19.95 cents at the close on Tuesday, but the September/December switch came under pressure, shrinking to 13.20 cents from 17.50 cents.
On the charts, traders said September faced near-term support at 160.00, with the next downside hurdles at 158.00 and 155.00 cents. Resistance was seen at 165.00 cents.

London robusta futures were broadly lower at midday on Friday, but steady roaster buying stemmed losses. At the break, benchmark September stood $25 weaker at $1,746, after ranging from $1,758 to $1,745.
